stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to 90% speedup according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher quality model output, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows in AI applications.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, promising faster local AI inference.
This is currently available in a preview state, indicating active development and optimization.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, ensuring all processing runs directly on the user's device.
The core value proposition is providing private, on-device AI assistance for coding tasks.

stories.title: Google is better at playing the AI regulations game
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: The EU has mandated that Google must grant greater access to Android for its AI competitors.
This regulatory action forces Google to change its long-standing resistance to open access on its platform.
The story highlights the increasing regulatory pressure on major tech players regarding AI competition.

stories.title: Roblox will let people use AI to make games on their phone
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Roblox is integrating AI tools directly into its mobile application for game creation.
This move signals a significant embrace of generative AI within a major gaming platform.
The feature raises concerns about potential content quality overload on the platform.

stories.title: Energy IPOs surge as investors hunt for ways to play AI boom
stories.author: Martha Muir in New York
bullet_points: Energy sector IPOs are experiencing a significant surge in market activity.
The increased investment interest is linked to investors seeking exposure to the AI boom.
Companies are raising capital at the fastest pace observed in the current century.

stories.title: Early Adoption of Agentic Coding Tools by GitHub Projects
stories.author: Daqing Hou
bullet_points: Agentic coding tools are advancing to the point of autonomously generating and submitting pull requests (PRs).
The research shifts focus from individual PR outcomes to the broader adoption and management of these tools at the project level.
The study analyzes a large dataset of over 25,000 agent-generated PRs across numerous popular GitHub repositories.

stories.title: Rethinking Penetration Testing for AI-Enabled Systems: From Resource Compromise to Behavioral Objective Violation
stories.author: Moslem Attar-Raouf
bullet_points: Traditional penetration testing is insufficient for AI-enabled systems.
Adversaries can now influence system behavior through non-traditional vectors like prompts, training data, or sensor inputs.
The focus of security testing must shift from resource compromise to behavioral objective violation in AI.

stories.title: Early Adoption of Agentic Coding Tools by GitHub Projects
stories.author: Daqing Hou
bullet_points: Investigates the project-level adoption and management of agentic coding tools, moving beyond simple PR outcomes.
Analyzes a large dataset of 25,264 agentic Pull Requests across 2,361 popular GitHub repositories.
Highlights a significant shift in software development towards human-agent collaboration facilitated by increasingly capable coding agents.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces significant performance improvements.
Enhanced GGUF model compatibility is now available via llama.cpp integration.
The update broadens model support across various hardware, complementing the MLX engine on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: New York governor says she’s using AI to analyze ‘every single rule’ in the state
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: NY Governor Hochul is deploying AI to analyze all state rules, regulations, and policies.
The initiative represents a governmental application of AI for regulatory review and modernization.
This usage occurs alongside a potential moratorium on new AI data centers in the state.

stories.title: Google is renaming NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Google is rebranding its AI note-taking application from NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook.
The app will continue to operate as a standalone product despite deeper integration with Gemini and Google Search.
The feature was initially revealed in May 2023 under the codename Project Tailwind.

stories.title: Tesla driver in fatal Texas crash overrode FSD by pressing accelerator ‘100 percent,’ investigators confirm
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: NTSB preliminary report confirms a Tesla driver manually overrode Full Self-Driving (FSD) in a fatal Texas crash.
The driver was found to have pressed the accelerator to 100 percent, overriding the vehicle's automated systems.
The investigation involved examining the electronic data from the Tesla Model 3 involved in the incident.

stories.title: Apple’s OLED iPad Mini upgrade is on the way as prices continue to rise
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Apple's iPad Mini is rumored to receive an OLED display upgrade.
The potential upgrade is anticipated as early as October, according to Mark Gurman.
This would represent the most substantial refresh for the iPad Mini since its 2021 model.

stories.title: ‘No company is going to go to jail for you’: Proton’s CTO on balancing privacy, policy, and trust
stories.author: Nilay Patel
bullet_points: The article features an interview with Proton's CTO, Bart Butler, discussing the complexities of privacy, policy, and user trust.
Proton is highlighted as a provider of private and secure productivity software, including Proton Mail and Proton Docs.
A key theme discussed is the legal and operational boundaries regarding user data, summarized by the CTO's statement about corporate liability.

stories.title: We've seen helium baked off a rocky exoplanet's atmosphere
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: Astronomers have detected the loss of helium from the atmosphere of a rocky exoplanet.
The observation allows scientists to infer the composition of the remaining atmospheric gases.
This research contributes to the understanding of planetary atmospheric evolution outside our solar system.

stories.title: OnePlus confirms shutdown in the US and Europe, ending months of speculation
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: OnePlus has officially confirmed the shutdown of its operations in the US and Europe.
The announcement ends a period of speculation regarding the company's regional presence.
The company has committed to providing continued support for all previously released OnePlus devices.

stories.title: Tesla driver who blamed crash on autopilot pressed accelerator 100%, NTSB finds
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: NTSB investigation concluded that the Tesla driver manually overrode the Full Self-Driving (FSD) system during the crash.
The findings support Elon Musk's assertion that the driver was in control and actively engaged with the vehicle.
The incident highlights ongoing regulatory and safety scrutiny surrounding advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) like Tesla's Autopilot/FSD.

stories.title: Move over, GPS: Navigation satellites in low-Earth orbit are making a comeback
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Xona is developing a new satellite navigation system to compete with GPS.
The system plans to deploy 258 satellites into low-Earth orbit (LEO).
This represents a potential shift or alternative to established global positioning services.

stories.title: Deep Interaction: An Efficient Human-AI Interaction Method for Large Reasoning Models
stories.author: Jie Li
bullet_points: Addresses the limitations of current LLM interaction when Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning fails.
Proposes a new method, 'Deep Interaction,' to improve efficiency in human-AI dialogue during complex tasks.
Aims to move beyond simple regeneration or manual error flagging in multi-step reasoning.

stories.title: AI-accelerated End-to-End Framework for Rapid Professional Upskilling
stories.author: Robert Ogburn
bullet_points: Addresses the critical industry problem of slow enterprise skills gap closure amidst massive workforce reskilling needs by 2030.
Introduces an end-to-end framework that applies AI acceleration across five distinct stages of the upskilling lifecycle.
Aims to improve upon existing frameworks by integrating AI across knowledge acquisition, content development, teaching, and assessment.

stories.title: Transforming Rank: How Architecture Navigates the Spectral Pathologies of Depth
stories.author: Katie Everett
bullet_points: The research analyzes how Transformer architecture components influence the preservation of 'rank' across network depth.
It reinterprets skip connections and normalization not just as magnitude controllers, but as mechanisms to maintain gradient rank.
The study demonstrates that standard expressive operations (matrix multiplications, nonlinearities) inherently reduce network rank.

stories.title: Do Agent Optimizers Compound? A Continual-Learning Evaluation on Terminal-Bench 2.0
stories.author: Soheil Feizi
bullet_points: The paper investigates whether gains from agent-optimization methods are cumulative (compound) over time.
Current reporting often treats optimization gains as one-shot, failing to model real-world, recursive optimization needs.
The research uses Terminal-Bench 2.0 to evaluate how agents perform after repeated optimization cycles.

stories.title: The Dynamic Verifiable Multi-Agent Human Agentic Loyalty Loop (DVM-HALL) Model and the Net Human-Agent Score (NHAS) in Autonomous Commerce
stories.author: Daya Shankar
bullet_points: The paper addresses the disruption of traditional customer loyalty models due to the rise of autonomous, goal-directed AI agents.
It introduces the Dynamic Verifiable Multi-Agent Human Agentic Loyalty Loop (DVM-HALL) model.
A new metric, the Net Human-Agent Score (NHAS), is proposed to evaluate human-agent relationships in autonomous commerce.

stories.title: Leveraging unlabelled data for generalizable neural population decoding
stories.author: Guillaume Lajoie
bullet_points: The research addresses a key limitation in neurotechnology decoding: the reliance on supervised learning (SL) which requires paired behavioral labels.
The proposed method, MOJO (Masked autOencoder-based), leverages unlabelled neural data to improve decoder robustness and generalization.
This work is highly relevant to advancing brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) and closed-loop neurotechnologies by enabling training on larger, unlabeled datasets.

stories.title: MetaPerch: Learning from metadata for bioacoustics foundation models
stories.author: Jenny Hamer
bullet_points: The research introduces MetaPerch, a method to enhance bioacoustic foundation models.
It leverages readily available recording metadata (e.g., location, time) as auxiliary supervision.
This aims to unlock untapped potential beyond relying solely on raw audio data from large citizen science platforms.

stories.title: Screening of Biosecurity Features in Metagenomic Data with Evo 2 Probes
stories.author: Vanessa Smilansky
bullet_points: The research investigates the utility of genomic foundation models (like Evo 2) for biosecurity screening.
The study uses minimal linear and attention probes on frozen model activations to extract biosecurity-relevant signals without retraining the large model.
The probes demonstrated strong discrimination in detecting antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in metagenomic data.

stories.title: Transforming Rank: How Architecture Navigates the Spectral Pathologies of Depth
stories.author: Katie Everett
bullet_points: The research analyzes how Transformer architecture components influence the preservation of matrix rank across network depth during initialization.
It reinterprets skip connections and normalization not just as magnitude controllers, but as mechanisms for maintaining gradient rank.
The study suggests a trade-off exists where skip connections balance rank collapse against ensemble-like properties.

stories.title: Do Agent Optimizers Compound? A Continual-Learning Evaluation on Terminal-Bench 2.0
stories.author: Soheil Feizi
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical gap in agent optimization research: the assumption that gains are one-shot.
It investigates whether improvements from agent optimizers can compound when optimization is applied recursively over time.
The study uses Terminal-Bench 2.0 to evaluate the stability and long-term efficacy of optimization methods in dynamic environments.

stories.title: Hindcast: Replaying Prediction Markets to Evaluate LLM Forecasters
stories.author: Ben Zhou
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'Hindcast' to rigorously evaluate Large Language Model (LLM) forecasters using prediction market backtesting.
It identifies two critical data leakage issues in LLM forecasting evaluations: retrieval models accessing post-event reports and training data contamination.
This work highlights methodological challenges in accurately testing the predictive capabilities of LLMs against temporal biases.

stories.title: Can an Old Dog Be Taught New Tricks? Taking LLMs Beyond Sentence Level Translation
stories.author: Alaina Brandt
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitation of current machine translation systems treating translation as a sentence-by-sentence task.
It introduces PAT (Pragmatic Auto-Translator), a RAG-based system designed for whole-document, corpus-informed translation.
The system leverages context from comparable longform texts in U.S. English and Latin American Spanish to improve translation quality.

stories.title: DeepStress: Stress-Testing Deep Search Agents
stories.author: Frederic Bechet
bullet_points: Introduces DeepStress, a new framework designed to stress-test deep search agents.
Addresses the gap in current research regarding the robustness of search agents when faced with poor-quality evidence.
Simulates challenging evidence by replacing the retrieval module with a controlled synthetic environment.

stories.title: SPyCE: Skill-Policy Co-evolution for Multimodal Agents
stories.author: Weijie Qiu
bullet_points: Introduces SPyCE, a method for Skill-Policy Co-evolution in multimodal agents.
Addresses limitations of current RL methods that treat trajectories as scalar rewards, hindering reusable tool-use discovery.
Proposes an approach that improves upon memory-based methods by updating the policy based on past experience, rather than relying solely on test-time retrieval.

stories.title: Post-Training Shifts Confidence: A Three-Stage Analysis of How SFT, RL, and OPD Shape Pre-, Intra-, and Post-CoT Calibration
stories.author: Xiaoyu Shen
bullet_points: The research analyzes how post-training methods (SFT, RL, OPD) affect the confidence calibration of LLMs during reasoning.
It introduces a novel three-stage framework to evaluate confidence before, during, and after Chain-of-Thought (CoT) generation.
The study moves beyond simple final-answer accuracy to examine intermediate reasoning steps like difficulty estimation and early termination.

stories.title: Detecting LLM-Generated Texts with “Classical” Machine Learning
stories.author: uneven9434
bullet_points: The article discusses methods for detecting text generated by Large Language Models (LLMs).
The approach utilizes 'classical' machine learning techniques rather than solely relying on advanced LLM-specific detectors.
This suggests a potential shift or complementary approach in the field of AI content provenance and detection.

stories.title: OnePlus halts operations in USA and Europe
stories.author: pilililo2
bullet_points: OnePlus has ceased its operations within the United States and Europe.
The news originates from Hacker News, suggesting community interest in industry shifts.
The lack of detailed content limits the depth of the analysis, focusing only on the operational halt.

stories.title: Linus Torvalds on LLM usage in kernel development
stories.author: lore.kernel.org via thang
bullet_points: Linus Torvalds, a key figure in Linux development, has commented on the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) within the kernel development process.
The discussion likely addresses the practical implications, benefits, and potential risks of integrating AI tools into core operating system code.
This topic is relevant as it touches upon the future of software engineering and the adoption of generative AI in critical infrastructure.
